text:
Tract II has only 82 acres of irrigable land and Tract III has 680 acres. Most of the potential irrigable land is in the valleys of Sarpy Creek and the East Fort of Sarpy Creek. These areas are not planned for mining as most of the easily accessible coal has been eroded away. Therefore mining would have little effect on the irrigable lands of the area.
Grazing
The primary use of the entire lease and surrounding area is to produce forage for cattle, a few head of horses, and other domestic livestock. All of the identified vegetation types are grazed by domestic livestock or used by them for shelter, although the centers of denser stands of brush and timber may be penetrated occasionally. Forage production for the Project Area is typical for this area of southeastern Montana, averaging about 30 acres per animal unit. The grazing season is considered to be ten months. Forage for the additional two months is provided by locally grown and imported supplemental feeds, primarily alfalfa and alfalfa-grass hay. Thirty to forty-five acres are required to provide grazing for one mature cow with calf per year, at an average level of grazing management for the area. Intensive range improvement and management could increase the productivity of the native range lands by as much as 50 percent, or even more on the most productive sites.
Forestry
There are scattered stands of ponderosa pine throughout both tracts. Westmoreland Resources (1975 b) estimated that ponderosa pine stands with a canopy coverage from 25% to 100% occupied 23.7% of Tract III and 45.5% of Tract II.
